# Agent Terminal Panel

⌘⇧A: the session’s own agent as it runs, in its terminal, two-way.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The prompt and the agent button answer the pointer.

## The agent’s own screen

Every session Emaki runs has a terminal behind it: Claude Code’s hidden one, or Codex’s joined to its driver. This panel draws it whole, at the chat’s right, so you can watch the agent work as you would in the CLI, and type into it when you want to. It is the same terminal the window reads and types into, so nothing is doubled.

Open it with nothing running and it starts the agent (Claude Code); where one cannot start, a turn running in a terminal of your own, or an archived session, it says why. Whatever the agent asks that the window has no card for can be answered here. It shares the right side with the [shell terminal](../docs/shell.llms.md): one shows at a time.
